source: Verbatim from the SIT723 thesis (Table 2 and Table 6), locked for SIT724 so results stay comparable trimester-to-trimester.
scale: 1 (low) to 5 (high) per dimension; total score is out of 35 (7 dimensions x 5).

dimensions.name: Accuracy
dimensions.definition: Whether the feedback correctly identifies the bug or misconception and offers a valid path to resolution.

anchors.3: Partly correct / some important issue missing

dimensions.name: Selectivity
dimensions.definition: Whether the feedback avoids hallucinating non-existent problems or pointing to irrelevant issues in the student code.

anchors.3: Mostly selective but includes notable irrelevance
anchors.4: Selective and focused with minor irrelevance

dimensions.name: Clarity
dimensions.definition: Whether the feedback is easy for a beginner Python learner to understand.

anchors.5: Very clear, accessible, and easy to follow

dimensions.name: Informativeness
dimensions.definition: Whether the feedback gives enough useful information to help the learner move forward.

anchors.4: Helpful and gives a clear path forward
anchors.5: Highly useful, well-explained, and strongly guiding

dimensions.name: Specificity
dimensions.definition: Whether the feedback addresses the student's actual code, mistake, or misconception rather than providing generic advice.

anchors.2: Weakly connected to the actual issue
anchors.4: Clearly tied to the student's mistake
anchors.5: Precisely targeted to the actual misconception and code context

dimensions.name: Level of Detail
dimensions.definition: Whether the feedback gives the right amount of guidance without being too vague or giving away the answer completely.

anchors.5: Excellent balance / guides thinking without over-solving

dimensions.name: Ethics & Safety
dimensions.definition: Whether the feedback avoids unsafe, overconfident, or misleading advice and encourages responsible verification where appropriate.
